title: Escape: Clonal Evolution & Resistance
description: A tumour is a population, and populations evolve. Every treatment selects the few cells that happen to resist it; they inherit the tumour. Drug resistance is not learned but chosen - by the treatment itself. Unlocks the Resistant Clone Colony.

puzzle.goal: A tumour holds n clones; clone i makes up a fraction x_i of it and has fitness f_i - its net growth rate under the current treatment. A clone grows in share only if it is fitter than the tumour's average. Write how the fraction of clone i changes.
puzzle.name: replicator equation (selection among competing clones)
puzzle.form: x _ i * ( f _ i - sum ( j , 1 , n , x _ j * f _ j ) )
puzzle.expr: x * exp ( s * t ) / ( 1 - x + x * exp ( s * t ) )
puzzle.ask: A resistant clone starts as a fraction x and grows faster than the rest by s per day under treatment; its share is then x e^{st}/(1 − x + x e^{st}). Find its share after t days.

vars.x: fraction of the tumour (x in step 2: the resistant clone's starting share)
vars.s: fitness advantage of the resistant clone (per day)

puzzle.method: Each clone grows as dN_i/dt = f_i N_i. Differentiate x_i = N_i/ΣN_j with the quotient rule; the denominator brings in the mean fitness.
